rows.hebrew: הֲ/לָהֵ֣ן תְּשַׂבֵּ֗רְנָה עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגְדָּ֔לוּ הֲ/לָהֵן֙ תֵּֽעָגֵ֔נָה לְ/בִלְתִּ֖י הֱי֣וֹת לְ/אִ֑ישׁ אַ֣ל בְּנֹתַ֗/י כִּֽי מַר לִ֤/י מְאֹד֙ מִ/כֶּ֔ם כִּֽי יָצְאָ֥ה בִ֖/י יַד יְהוָֽה
rows.after: would you wait until they grew up? Would you keep yourselves from marrying for their sake? No, my daughters. My bitterness is greater than yours, for the LORD’s hand has turned against me.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ שָׁ֣בָה יְבִמְתֵּ֔/ךְ אֶל עַמָּ֖/הּ וְ/אֶל אֱלֹהֶ֑י/הָ שׁ֖וּבִי אַחֲרֵ֥י יְבִמְתֵּֽ/ךְ
rows.after: Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. Return with her.”

rows.hebrew: בַּ/אֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּמ֨וּתִי֙ אָמ֔וּת וְ/שָׁ֖ם אֶקָּבֵ֑ר כֹּה֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה יְהוָ֥ה לִ/י֙ וְ/כֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י הַ/מָּ֔וֶת יַפְרִ֖יד בֵּינִ֥/י וּ/בֵינֵֽ/ךְ
rows.after: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do this to me, and more besides, if anything but death separates you and me.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵי/הֶ֔ן אַל תִּקְרֶ֥אנָה לִ֖/י נָעֳמִ֑י קְרֶ֤אןָ לִ/י֙ מָרָ֔א כִּי הֵמַ֥ר שַׁדַּ֛י לִ֖/י מְאֹֽד
rows.after: She answered, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has made my life deeply bitter.

rows.hebrew: אֲנִי֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וְ/רֵיקָ֖ם הֱשִׁיבַ֣/נִי יְהוָ֑ה לָ֣/מָּה תִקְרֶ֤אנָה לִ/י֙ נָעֳמִ֔י וַֽ/יהוָה֙ עָ֣נָה בִ֔/י וְ/שַׁדַּ֖י הֵ֥רַֽע לִֽ/י
annotations: <note n="C">We read one or more accents in L differently from BHQ. </note>
<note n="c">We read one or more accents in L differently than BHS. Often this notation indicates a typographical error in BHS. </note>
rows.after: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought disaster on me?”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּ֗אמֶר אֲלַקֳטָה נָּא֙ וְ/אָסַפְתִּ֣י בָֽ/עֳמָרִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י הַ/קּוֹצְרִ֑ים וַ/תָּב֣וֹא וַֽ/תַּעֲמ֗וֹד מֵ/אָ֤ז הַ/בֹּ֨קֶר֙ וְ/עַד עַ֔תָּה זֶ֛ה שִׁבְתָּ֥/הּ הַ/בַּ֖יִת מְעָֽט
rows.after: She asked, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.’ She came this morning and has stayed until now, with only a short rest in the shelter.”

rows.hebrew: עֵינַ֜יִ/ךְ בַּ/שָּׂדֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר יִקְצֹרוּ/ן֙ וְ/הָלַ֣כְתִּ אַחֲרֵי/הֶ֔ן הֲ/ל֥וֹא צִוִּ֛יתִי אֶת הַ/נְּעָרִ֖ים לְ/בִלְתִּ֣י נָגְעֵ֑/ךְ וְ/צָמִ֗ת וְ/הָלַכְתְּ֙ אֶל הַ/כֵּלִ֔ים וְ/שָׁתִ֕ית מֵ/אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאֲב֖וּ/ן הַ/נְּעָרִֽים
annotations: <note n="Q">Marks a place where we agree with BHQ against BHS in reading L. </note>
<note n="v">We read one or more vowels in L differently from BHS. </note>
rows.after: Watch the field they are harvesting and follow the women. I have ordered the young men not to touch you. When you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink what the young men have drawn.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְ/כַלָּתָ֗/הּ בָּר֥וּךְ הוּא֙ לַ/יהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא עָזַ֣ב חַסְדּ֔/וֹ אֶת הַ/חַיִּ֖ים וְ/אֶת הַ/מֵּתִ֑ים וַ/תֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣/הּ נָעֳמִ֗י קָר֥וֹב לָ֨/נוּ֙ הָ/אִ֔ישׁ מִֽ/גֹּאֲלֵ֖/נוּ הֽוּא
rows.after: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not abandoned his steadfast love for the living and the dead.” Then she added, “The man is related to us. He is one of our redeemers.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּ֥אמֶר נָעֳמִ֖י אֶל ר֣וּת כַּלָּתָ֑/הּ ט֣וֹב בִּתִּ֗/י כִּ֤י תֵֽצְאִי֙ עִם נַ֣עֲרוֹתָ֔י/ו וְ/לֹ֥א יִפְגְּעוּ בָ֖/ךְ בְּ/שָׂדֶ֥ה אַחֵֽר
rows.after: Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, for you to go out with his young women. In another field someone might assault you.”

rows.hebrew: וְ/רָחַ֣צְתְּ וָ/סַ֗כְתְּ וְ/שַׂ֧מְתְּ שמלת/ך עָלַ֖יִ/ךְ ו/ירדתי הַ/גֹּ֑רֶן אַל תִּוָּדְעִ֣י לָ/אִ֔ישׁ עַ֥ד כַּלֹּת֖/וֹ לֶ/אֱכֹ֥ל וְ/לִ/שְׁתּֽוֹת
rows.after: Wash, put on oil, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.

rows.hebrew: וִ/יהִ֣י בְ/שָׁכְב֗/וֹ וְ/יָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ אֶת הַ/מָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁכַּב שָׁ֔ם וּ/בָ֛את וְ/גִלִּ֥ית מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖י/ו ו/שכבתי וְ/הוּא֙ יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔/ךְ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעַשִֽׂי/ן
annotations: <note n="V">We read one or more vowels in L differently from BHQ. </note>
rows.after: When he lies down, notice where he is lying. Then go in, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֖אמֶר מִי אָ֑תּ וַ/תֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ ר֣וּת אֲמָתֶ֔/ךָ וּ/פָרַשְׂתָּ֤ כְנָפֶ֨/ךָ֙ עַל אֲמָ֣תְ/ךָ֔ כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה
annotations: <note n="U">We agree with both BHS 1997 and BHQ on an unexpected reading. </note>
rows.after: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am Ruth, your servant,” she replied. “Spread the wing of your garment over your servant, for you are a redeemer.”

rows.hebrew: וְ/עַתָּה֙ כִּ֣י אָמְנָ֔ם כִּ֥י אם גֹאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי וְ/גַ֛ם יֵ֥שׁ גֹּאֵ֖ל קָר֥וֹב מִמֶּֽ/נִּי
rows.after: It is true that I am a redeemer, but there is another redeemer more closely related than I am.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֗אמֶר הָ֠בִי הַ/מִּטְפַּ֧חַת אֲשֶׁר עָלַ֛יִ/ךְ וְ/אֶֽחֳזִי בָ֖/הּ וַ/תֹּ֣אחֶז בָּ֑/הּ וַ/יָּ֤מָד שֵׁשׁ שְׂעֹרִים֙ וַ/יָּ֣שֶׁת עָלֶ֔י/הָ וַ/יָּבֹ֖א הָ/עִֽיר
rows.after: He said, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” She held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and lifted the load onto her. Then he went into town.

rows.hebrew: וּ/בֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַ/שַּׁעַר֮ וַ/יֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁם֒ וְ/הִנֵּ֨ה הַ/גֹּאֵ֤ל עֹבֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר בֹּ֔עַז וַ/יֹּ֛אמֶר ס֥וּרָ/ה שְׁבָ/ה פֹּ֖ה פְּלֹנִ֣י אַלְמֹנִ֑י וַ/יָּ֖סַר וַ/יֵּשֵֽׁב
rows.after: Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down. Just then the redeemer he had spoken of passed by. “Come over and sit here, so-and-so,” Boaz called. The man came over and sat down.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַ/גֹּאֵ֔ל חֶלְקַת֙ הַ/שָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְ/אָחִ֖י/נוּ לֶ/אֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ מָכְרָ֣ה נָעֳמִ֔י הַ/שָּׁ֖בָה מִ/שְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב
rows.after: He told the redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.

rows.hebrew: וַ/אֲנִ֨י אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֶגְלֶ֧ה אָזְנְ/ךָ֣ לֵ/אמֹ֗ר קְ֠נֵה נֶ֥גֶד הַֽ/יֹּשְׁבִים֮ וְ/נֶ֣גֶד זִקְנֵ֣י עַמִּ/י֒ אִם תִּגְאַל֙ גְּאָ֔ל וְ/אִם לֹ֨א יִגְאַ֜ל הַגִּ֣ידָ/ה לִּ֗/י ו/אדע כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין זוּלָֽתְ/ךָ֙ לִ/גְא֔וֹל וְ/אָנֹכִ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑י/ךָ וַ/יֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י אֶגְאָֽל
rows.after: I thought I should bring it to your attention: buy it here before those seated with us and the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, do so. If it is not to be redeemed, tell me so I will know. You have the first right to redeem it, and I come after you.” “I will redeem it,” the man said.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר בֹּ֔עַז בְּ/יוֹם קְנוֹתְ/ךָ֥ הַ/שָּׂדֶ֖ה מִ/יַּ֣ד נָעֳמִ֑י וּ֠/מֵ/אֵת ר֣וּת הַ/מּוֹאֲבִיָּ֤ה אֵֽשֶׁת הַ/מֵּת֙ קניתי לְ/הָקִ֥ים שֵׁם הַ/מֵּ֖ת עַל נַחֲלָתֽ/וֹ
rows.after: Then Boaz said, “On the day you acquire the field from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the dead man’s widow, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance.”

rows.hebrew: וְ/גַ֣ם אֶת ר֣וּת הַ/מֹּאֲבִיָּה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת מַחְל֜וֹן קָנִ֧יתִי לִ֣/י לְ/אִשָּׁ֗ה לְ/הָקִ֤ים שֵׁם הַ/מֵּת֙ עַל נַ֣חֲלָת֔/וֹ וְ/לֹא יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם הַ/מֵּ֛ת מֵ/עִ֥ם אֶחָ֖י/ו וּ/מִ/שַּׁ֣עַר מְקוֹמ֑/וֹ עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַ/יּֽוֹם
rows.after: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance. His name must not disappear from among his relatives or from the gate of his hometown. Today you are witnesses.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/תֹּאמַ֤רְנָה הַ/נָּשִׁים֙ אֶֽל נָעֳמִ֔י בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א הִשְׁבִּ֥ית לָ֛/ךְ גֹּאֵ֖ל הַ/יּ֑וֹם וְ/יִקָּרֵ֥א שְׁמ֖/וֹ בְּ/יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
rows.after: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you without a redeemer today! May his name be renowned in Israel.

rows.hebrew: וַ/תִּקַּ֨ח נָעֳמִ֤י אֶת הַ/יֶּ֨לֶד֙ וַ/תְּשִׁתֵ֣/הוּ בְ/חֵיקָ֔/הּ וַ/תְּהִי ל֖/וֹ לְ/אֹמֶֽנֶת
rows.after: Naomi took the child into her lap and became his caregiver.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עַמִּֽינָדָב֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת נַחְשׁ֔וֹן וְ/נַחְשׁ֖וֹן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת שַׂלְמָֽה
rows.after: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmah,
